title: Cuda graph batching & scheduling sweep — Nsight run notes
content:
Summary:

This note collects the results from a targeted sweep investigating interactions between CUDA graph-based capture, request batching behavior, and GPU/SM scheduling that appear to create intermittent utilization drops and 99th percentile token latency spikes on long-running hosted instances. Goal was to isolate whether scheduling behavior during rapid microbatch transitions (microbatch size 1-4) causes kernel launch gaps that degrade effective throughput, and to produce concrete mitigations.

Top-level findings (short):
- CUDA graph capture reduced host-side overhead but introduced periodic gaps when graph instance re-use collided with background stream work (metrics: 3–12% throughput variance across runs).
- Nsight timelines show short (~200–800us) gaps between graph-launched kernels where SM occupancy collapses; these coincide with sudden increases in CTAs queued and active warp scheduling stalls due to "device-side synchronization" and PCIe async memcpy queuing.
- Using a dedicated high-priority stream for graph launches (cudaStreamCreateWithPriority) cut gap frequency by ~70% in our controlled runs.
- Pre-warming graph instances + instantiating a pool sized to peak concurrency eliminated most of the observed 99p latency spikes in the lab, suggesting a reuse/instantiation race in current codepath.

Testbed setup:
- Machine: p4d-like dev rig (8x A100-sim), single GPU used for controlled runs to remove multi-GPU interferences.
- Driver/CUDA: NVIDIA driver 525.60, CUDA 12.1.
- Serving runtime: feature/graph-sweep branch (PR #842).
- Model: 13B decoder-only (sparse KV cache behavior triggered at token 128+), sequence length 512 for 95% of workload, variable bursts to 1024 for long prompts.
- Workload generator: synthetic permuted prompts producing microbatch sizes of 1, 2, 4, 8; request arrival pattern Poisson lambda matched to target qps.
- Profiling: NVIDIA Nsight Systems 2025.4 for long traces (60s windows) + Nsight Compute 2025.3 for representative kernel-level counters.

Run matrix (representative runs):
- A: baseline (no cuda graphs), microbatch 1, burst qps 120 (control)
- B: cuda-graph capture, graph-per-batch-size, microbatch 1, qps 120
- C: same as B + high-priority launch stream
- D: B + graph pool pre-warm (pool size = 4 concurrent graphs)
- E: B + async memcpy coalescing disabled

Key Nsight timeline observations:
- Kernel timeline patterns for B show regular clusters of 3-6 small kernels (attention, rotary, next_token) followed by a quiet window of ~300–900us where SM activity drops to background kernels only. These windows line up with CUDA graph instantiation calls (cudaGraphInstantiate) on the host thread.
- In many captures, the host thread calling instantiate is serializing with the runtime when graph cache lookup missed; host stalls appear to cause the driver to drain/flush work on the GPU before new graph execution, creating a perceptible gap in device-side scheduling.
- Nsight Compute counters during active windows: SM active cycles ~58–72%, achieved occupancy (active warps/warp per SM) 0.42–0.65. During gaps effective occupancy falls below 8% and stall reasons shift to "stall_data_dependency" and "stall_barrier" in some kernels.

Quantitative metrics (selected):
- Baseline A steady-state token throughput: 1100 tokens/s, 99p latency: 185ms.
- B (cuda graphs naive): avg throughput +6% (1166 tokens/s) but 99p latency regressed to 320ms with pronounced long-tail spikes. Variance across runs increased (std dev throughput +3x).
- C (high-priority stream): throughput similar to B, 99p latency improved to 210ms, long-tail spikes reduced ~70%.
- D (pre-warm pool): throughput +8% vs A and 99p latency 190ms; variance reduced to near-baseline.
- E (coalescing off): throughput dropped 4% and 99p latency unchanged; implies async memcpy behavior not the only root cause.

Hypotheses / Root causes considered:
1) Graph instantiation race: when a capture misses cache, the host-side instantiate call serializes with the CUDA runtime and causes device-side scheduling gaps.
2) Stream priority inversion: other lower-priority background work (metrics collectors, DMA copies) can preempt graph launches when using default streams.
3) Implicit device syncs triggered by certain driver/runtime interactions when graphs are destroyed/recreated under load.
4) Memory copy coalescing and pinned memory fragmentation can temporarily block DMA engine causing transient stalls seen as drop in SM utilization.

Evidence supporting hypotheses:
- Timeline correlation between cudaGraphInstantiate and gaps supports (1).
- Repro across machines and disabling unrelated background jobs reduced gap frequency for (2).
- Pre-warm pool eliminating the need for instantiation during steady-state removed most spikes (strong evidence for 1).

Repro commands and trace snippets used:
- Nsight systems capture (CLI):
  nsys profile --capture-range=cpu -t cuda,cuda_driver,cublas,cudnn --trace-filenames true --output graph-sweep-B run_serving --config config/sweep_b.json
- Minimal reproduce: run minimal harness that simulates capture miss:
  LD_PRELOAD=... ./graph_capture_harness --microbatch 1 --capture-miss-rate 0.2 --duration 120s
- Key flags tried in harness: graph_instance_cache=on/off, graph_pool_size=0/4/8, stream_priority=normal/high, async_memcpy_coalesce=on/off.

Short-term mitigations tested (and recommended):
- Pre-instantiate a pool of graph instances sized to expected concurrency (pool size = number of in-flight requests per GPU). This had the single biggest effect in lab runs. (Action: Evan to prototype a pool manager in runtime, ETA 2 weeks).
- Use high-priority stream for graph launches to reduce priority inversion (Action: Ruth to add optional flag to routing config to set stream priority; small change).
- Ensure graph instantiate path is asynchronous with respect to the hot serving thread: move infrequent instantiate/deinstantiate to a background worker where possible.

Longer-term considerations / possible engineering directions:
- Evaluate a persistent-kernel approach for the tight inner loop (single persistent kernel with work-queue) to remove graph lifecycle cost entirely. This is non-trivial for complex transformer kernels but could yield best tail-latency results.
- Work with driver team to see if graph instantiate can be made lock-free for execution-critical paths (file an upstream report if we can produce a minimized repro).
- Improve traceability: add metadata tags on graph instance creation and reuse events so correlation between host and device is easier in future Nsight captures.
- Investigate whether JIT kernel fusion (combine attention+ffn micro-kernels for small microbatches) increases sustained occupancy for microbatch=1 workloads.

Open questions we still have:
- Are specific models or sequence-length distributions more susceptible, beyond our 13B test? We need runs on smaller/bigger models.
- Is there an interaction with pinned memory fragmentation over long-lived processes that increases instantiate latency over time? (we saw some drift in later 10+ minute long runs)
- Does networked NVLink/NVSwitch topology materially change these patterns in multi-GPU deployment? We ran single-GPU in lab.

Action items (owners):
- Evan Zhang: prototype graph instance pool + background instantiate worker; measure 99p and throughput across microbatch sizes (2w).
- Ruth Kim: expose stream priority toggle + default to high for graph launches in dedicated mode; add config and docs (1w).
- Aisha Patel: run expanded sweep across 7B/70B variants and on multi-GPU infra to validate generality (2w).
- Diego Morales: create minimal repro and file upstream driver ticket if we can reliably trigger host-side serialize (JIRA-SE-2194 follow-up).

Appendix — quick Nsight/CUDA hints from this sweep:
- When capturing long traces, include cuda_driver and cuda_runtime to capture host-side driver calls (cudaGraphInstantiate shows up here).
- Use timeline markers in runtime (nvtx ranges) around graph cache lookup + instantiate to correlate easily.
- To debug priority inversion, temporarily add a noisy background memcpy loop on low-priority stream to see if graph launches are delayed.
- When possible, prefer graph instantiation at startup or scale-change time instead of on steady-state critical path.

Notes and miscellaneous:
- We observed a subtle difference between using one graph shape per microbatch-size versus an over-parameterized graph that handles variable seq lengths — the latter increased register pressure slightly but reduced instantiate rate and overall reduced 99p in our tests.
- Some traces show a tail of GPU-side "idle" time driven by host thread preemption in Linux (sched latency). Running the harness with SCHED_FIFO for the critical thread reduced occurrences in a few trials but has operational risk.

If you want the raw nsight captures and the harness logs they are uploaded to: s3://r-inference-profiles/graph-sweep/nov-2025/ (see CONFLUENCE-graphs link).

End of note.

-- Diego
